another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information!

Since Alex is 17 years old, I need to ask a few more questions to determine your eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (This includes A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQs up to level 3, or similar qualifications - but not apprenticeships in England.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school and hasn't started anything else yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Since Alex is 17 and has recently left education, there may still be a way to continue receiving Child Benefit for a limited period.

**Has Alex registered with either:**
- **A government-sponsored careers service**, or
- **The armed services**?

If so, you may be able to claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks while he's registered.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with a careers service or the armed forces. He just finished school but hasn't signed up for anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know.

I have a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex currently:**
- **Working 24 hours or more per week**, or
- **Receiving any benefits in his own right** (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working that much - he doesn't have a job at all right now. And he's not getting any benefits in his own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Just a couple more questions to confirm your eligibility:

1. **Do you live in the UK?**
2. **Does Alex live with you, or if not, are you contributing towards his upkeep (for example, food, clothes, or pocket money) at least equal to the Child Benefit amount?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. And yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming those details.

Based on the information you've provided, I now have enough to make an assessment. Let me summarise:

- Alex is 17 years old
- He is not currently in approved education or training
- He has not registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services
- He is not working 24+ hours per week
- He is not receiving benefits in his own right
- You live in the UK and Alex lives with you

Let me now provide you with my eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**For Alex (age 17):**
- Child Benefit normally stops when a child turns 16, unless they remain in approved education or training.
- Since Alex has finished school and is not currently in approved education or training, he doesn't meet this requirement.
- There is an option to continue Child Benefit for up to **20 weeks** if a 16 or 17 year old registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services – but Alex hasn't done this.

**What you could do:**
If Alex registers with a government-sponsored careers service (such as the National Careers Service in England), you may then be able to apply for Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks. Alternatively, if Alex returns to approved education or training before he turns 20, you could become eligible again at that point.

I hope this information is helpful. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
